<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, Inc. and Subsidiaries</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="NOTES_TO_CONSOLIDATED_FINANCIAL_STATEMEN">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">January 3, 2021, December 29, 2019 and December 30, 2018</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(Dollars in thousands except shares and per share amounts)</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000341" name="jax:OrganizationAndBusinessTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000341_dcnt_8c9c0eec-0b73-4822-8fa4-e8f448a0281d">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 1 &#8211; Organization and Business</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) was incorporated on <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000413" name="dei:EntityIncorporationDateOfIncorporation" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">August 15, 2014</ix:nonNumeric> in the state of Tennessee and is a holding company which is the sole managing member of and owns all of the outstanding Class A Units of J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC, the parent company of all of the Company&#8217;s operating subsidiaries. The Company is a publicly-traded company, with its stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol &#8220;JAX.&#8221; </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company, through J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC and its subsidiaries, owns and operates full service, upscale restaurants including J. Alexander&#8217;s, Redlands Grill, Overland Park Grill, Merus Grill and Stoney River Steakhouse and Grill (&#8220;Stoney River&#8221;).&#160;&#160;At January 3, 2021 and December 29, 2019, the Company operated <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxRestaurant" id="F_000414" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRestaurants" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="INF">46</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxRestaurant" id="F_000415" name="us-gaap:NumberOfRestaurants" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191229" decimals="INF">47</ix:nonFraction> restaurants, respectively, in <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxOperatingplace" id="F_000416" name="us-gaap:NumberOfStatesInWhichEntityOperates" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="INF"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxOperatingplace" id="F_000417" name="us-gaap:NumberOfStatesInWhichEntityOperates" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191229" decimals="INF">16</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> states.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s restaurants are concentrated primarily in the East, Southeast, and Midwest regions of the United States.&#160;&#160;The Company does not have any restaurants operating under franchise agreements.<span style="font-size:12pt;">&#160;</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Effects of COVID-19</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 30, 2020, the World Health Organization (&#8220;WHO&#8221;) announced a global health emergency due to the global spread of a new strain of coronavirus (&#8220;COVID-19&#8221;) and the related risks to the international community. On March 11, 2020, the WHO classified the COVID-19 outbreak as a pandemic, and on March 13, 2020 the United States declared the pandemic a National Public Health Emergency.&#160;&#160;In response, many states and jurisdictions in which the Company operates restaurants issued stay-at-home orders and other measures, including the closure of all in-restaurant dining, aimed at slowing the spread of the virus beginning in March 2020. These measures resulted in the closure of the Company&#8217;s dining rooms beginning in mid-March 2020 and a shift to an off&#8209;premise operations platform only until late April 2020 when certain states began to allow for partial reopening of dining rooms.&#160;&#160;Dining room capacity restrictions remain in place at varying degrees while a limited number of locations are operating at full capacity in accordance with their state&#8217;s or local government&#8217;s guidelines through the date of this report.&#160;&#160;As a result of the government&#8209;mandated restrictions and related public concerns, the Company&#8217;s net sales, results of operations and cash flows were negatively impacted during fiscal year 2020 due to significant reductions in guest counts. The Company has taken measures to increase its off-premise sales during the COVID-19 pandemic, including implementing its online ordering platform, introducing curbside service, menu innovation which includes family-style meals and butcher-shop sales of cook-at-home, hand-cut steaks and whole loins, and increasing digital marketing and email campaigns to drive guest awareness.&#160;&#160;Further, the Company began implementing contactless payment in 2020 as well as utilizing paperless menus to enhance the safety of our guests and employees in the restaurant. Additionally, the Company has invested in pub and booth partitions to increase capacity while maintaining guest safety.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition to the decline in restaurant sales, the Company also incurred approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000418" name="jax:CostIncurredDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapLiabilityForCatastropheClaimsByCatastrophicEventAxis_jaxCoronavirusMember_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">3,444</ix:nonFraction> of costs directly related to the COVID-19 pandemic in fiscal 2020, which consists primarily of benefits and payments to furloughed restaurant employees for emergency sick leave, vacation and other sick leave benefits and related payroll taxes as well as inventory waste. Additionally, the Company continued to incur expenses related to the ongoing operations of the restaurants as well as monthly rent and occupancy&#8209;related costs during the period that its restaurants were temporarily closed or operating on an off-premise basis only or with limited capacity. The Company has implemented measures to reduce its costs and limit its cash outflows during the COVID-19 pandemic, including temporary reductions in staffing levels and related furloughs of restaurant-level hourly employees, elimination of certain positions at the Company&#8217;s corporate office, deferral or cancellation of significant capital expenditure projects, engaging in negotiations with vendors and landlords regarding deferral or abatement of rental and other contractual obligations and the deferral of tax payments where allowed. The Company executed deferral and abatement agreements for certain of its locations with landlords during each of the last three quarters of 2020.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The disruption in operations and reduction in restaurant sales also led the Company to consider the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the recoverability of its assets, including property and equipment, right-of-use assets for operating leases, goodwill and intangible assets, and others. Such impairment analyses resulted in the Company recording impairment charges totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000419" name="us-gaap:AssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">16,426</ix:nonFraction> for the year ended January 3, 2021, which are discussed further in Notes 2(h) and 2(i) below. The ultimate severity and longevity of the COVID-19 pandemic is unknown, and therefore, it is possible that additional impairments could be identified in future periods, and such amounts could be material.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">58</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000341_dcnt_8c9c0eec-0b73-4822-8fa4-e8f448a0281d">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">To preserve financial flexibility, the Company drew down the remaining $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000420" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromLongTermLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_jaxDevelopmentLineOfCreditMember_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">17,000</ix:nonFraction> of available capacity (at the time of the draw) under its revolving credit facility in March 2020. During April 2020, the Company also entered into deferral letter agreements with its lender to postpone principal and interest payments on its outstanding indebtedness for a period of 90 days and, in June 2020, an additional deferral letter was entered into to defer principal payments for an additional 90-day period. Additionally, the Company entered into a modification agreement in April 2020 to defer the maturity of, and interest payments under, one of its term loans to September 2021 (which was subsequently modified again in October 2020 as discussed below). In May 2020, the Company obtained a waiver letter from its lender that waived existing financial covenants and instituted new financial covenants. In June 2020, the Company entered into an amendment with its lender to increase the borrowing capacity under its revolving line of credit by an additional $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000421" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityRemainingBorrowingCapacity" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapTypeOfArrangementAxis_jaxModificationAgreementMember_20200628" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">15,000</ix:nonFraction>. In October 2020, the Company entered into an agreement with its lender which extended the maturity dates of certain of its outstanding loans along with other modifications including instituting new financial covenants as well as repaid $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000422" name="us-gaap:RepaymentsOfLongTermLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_jaxDevelopmentLineOfCreditMember_20201028_20201028" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">10,000</ix:nonFraction> of the $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000423" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromLongTermLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">17,000</ix:nonFraction> borrowed in March 2020.&#160;&#160;See Note 10 &#8211; Debt for further discussion.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On March 27, 2020, the Coronavirus Aid Relief and Economic Security Act (&#8220;CARES Act&#8221;) was enacted into law. The CARES Act is a tax and spending package intended to provide economic relief to address the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The CARES Act includes several significant income tax provisions that are addressed in Note 14 &#8211; Income Taxes below. Additionally, the CARES Act provides for deferred payment of the employer portion of social security taxes through the end of calendar 2020, with <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000424" name="jax:PercentageOfDeferredPaymentOfEmployerPortionOfSocialSecurityTaxesYearOneCARESAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% of the deferred amount due December 31, 2021 and the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000425" name="jax:PercentageOfDeferredPaymentOfEmployerPortionOfSocialSecurityTaxesYearTwoCARESAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% due December 31, 2022. As of the fiscal year ended January 3, 2021, the Company has deferred the payment of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000426" name="jax:EmployerPortionOfAccruedSocialSecurityTaxesUnderCARESAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">3,593</ix:nonFraction> of social security taxes, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000427" name="jax:EmployerPortionOfAccruedSocialSecurityTaxesNoncurrentUnderCARESAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapBalanceSheetLocationAxis_us-gaapOtherNoncurrentLiabilitiesMember_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,796</ix:nonFraction> of which is accrued within &#8220;Other long-term liabilities&#8221; (see Note 11 &#8211; Other Long-Term Liabilities) while the current portion of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000428" name="jax:EmployerPortionOfAccruedSocialSecurityTaxesCurrentUnderCARESAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapBalanceSheetLocationAxis_jaxAccruedExpensesAndOtherCurrentLiabilitiesMember_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,796</ix:nonFraction> is included in &#8220;Accrued expenses and other current liabilities&#8221; (see Note 9 &#8211; Accrued Expenses and Other Current Liabilities) in the Consolidated Balance Sheet. Further, the CARES Act provides an employee retention credit (&#8220;ERC&#8221;), which is a refundable tax credit against certain employment taxes of up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000429" name="jax:RefundableTaxCreditForEmploymentTaxesUnderCaresAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">5</ix:nonFraction> per employee for eligible employers. The tax credit is equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000430" name="jax:PercentageOfRefundableTaxCreditUnderCaresAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% of qualified wages paid to employees during a quarter, capped at $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000431" name="jax:RefundableTaxCreditCappedOfQualifiedWagesPerEmployeeUnderCaresAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">10</ix:nonFraction> of qualified wages per employee through the end of 2020. During fiscal year 2020, the Company determined that it was an eligible employer for purposes of the ERC and further determined that during the first three quarters of fiscal 2020 it had paid qualified wages of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000432" name="jax:RefundableTaxCreditQualifiedWagesPaidUnderCaresAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20200927" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">2,010</ix:nonFraction> for which it intends to file amended payroll tax returns to claim as refunds. In fiscal 2020, based on the available accounting guidance, the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000433" name="jax:RecognitionOfRefundableTaxCreditUnderCaresAct" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">1,082</ix:nonFraction> receivable which represents the amount determined to be probable of realization related to the ERC as a reduction to &#8220;Restaurant labor and related costs&#8221; on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income and in &#8220;Accounts and other receivables&#8221; on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheet (See Note 2(e)) for the year ended January 3, 2021.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The full impact of the COVID-19 pandemic continues to evolve as of the date of this report. Given the uncertainty surrounding the global economy and governmental restrictions on the Company&#8217;s operations, the Company cannot reasonably predict when its restaurants will be able to return to normal dining room operations. Due to the rapid development and fluidity of this situation, the Company cannot determine the ultimate impact that the COVID-19 pandemic will have on its consolidated financial condition, liquidity and future results of operations, and therefore any prediction as to the ultimate material adverse impact on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial condition, liquidity, and future results of operations is uncertain. The Company does expect that its results of operations, cash flows and liquidity will be negatively affected by the pandemic during fiscal 2021.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000342" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_7f01ef7a-7479-48a3-b1c7-cd7eceacde9a">

All intercompany profits, transactions, and balances between the Company and its subsidiaries have been eliminated. It is the Company&#8217;s policy to reclassify prior year amounts to conform to the current year&#8217;s presentation for comparative purposes, if such a reclassification is warranted.</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounts receivable are primarily related to amounts due from various taxing jurisdictions, third-party online gift card sellers</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and expected workers&#8217; compensation rebates and vendor rebates which have been earned but not yet received. Additionally,</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">as discussed in Note 1 &#8211; &#8220;Organization and Business&#8221; above, the Company recorded a receivable in fiscal 2020 related to the</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">discussed in Note 14 &#8211; Income Taxes. Due to the nature of the entities involved, the nature of the receivables and its past</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">history with such receivables, the Company believes that an additional allowance against these recorded amounts is not</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">warranted.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000368" name="us-gaap:InventoryPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true">
<div style="align:left;">

<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:2.5%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">f)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Inventories</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">Inventories are stated at the lower of cost or net realizable value, with cost being determined using an average cost method</span><span style="color:#000000;">.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At the beginning of fiscal 2020, the Company implemented a new inventory management system. In connection with this implementation, the Company changed its method of accounting for inventory from the lower of cost (first-in, first-out) or net realizable value method utilized by its legacy system to the lower of cost or net realizable value method, with cost being determined using an average cost method, effective December 30, 2019 (the first day of the current fiscal year). The Company believes this change in accounting principle is preferable, as it will result in greater precision in the costing of inventories. In addition, the average cost method better aligns with the functionality of the new inventory management system. The Company determined that the effects of adopting the average cost method were not material to its Consolidated Financial Statements. Prior to the conversion to the new inventory management system, the Company was not able to determine the impact of the change to the average cost method. Therefore, it did not retroactively apply the change to periods prior to fiscal year 2020.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000369" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true">
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:2.5%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.17%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">g)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Property and Equipment, Net</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company states property and equipment at cost less accumulated depreciation and amortization. Depreciation and amortization expense is calculated using the straight&#8209;line method. The useful lives of assets are typically <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000437" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapLandBuildingsAndImprovementsMember_20191230_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_e5c8dbb8-2e8f-4135-8bcf-f3ede8973d85">30</ix:nonNumeric>-<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000438" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapLandBuildingsAndImprovementsMember_20191230_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">40<ix:continuation id="C_e5c8dbb8-2e8f-4135-8bcf-f3ede8973d85"> years</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric> for buildings and land improvements and <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000439" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapFurnitureAndFixturesMember_20191230_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_066e1f57-64e6-45e8-b5d6-f4842e32f9ad">two</ix:nonNumeric>-<ix:nonNumeric id="F_000440" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis_us-gaapFurnitureAndFixturesMember_20191230_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">10<ix:continuation id="C_066e1f57-64e6-45e8-b5d6-f4842e32f9ad"> years</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric> for furniture, fixtures, and equipment. Leasehold improvements are amortized over the lesser of the useful life or the remaining lease term, generally inclusive of renewal periods. Gains or losses are recognized upon the disposal of property and equipment, and the asset and related accumulated depreciation and amortization are removed from the accounts. Maintenance, repairs and betterments that do not enhance the value of or increase the life of the assets are expensed as incurred. The Company capitalizes all direct external costs associated with obtaining the land, building, and equipment for each new restaurant, as well as construction period interest. All direct external costs associated with obtaining the dining room and kitchen equipment, signage, and other assets and equipment are also capitalized.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain direct and indirect costs are capitalized as building and leasehold improvement costs in conjunction with capital improvement projects at existing restaurants and acquiring and developing new restaurant sites. Such costs are amortized over the life of the related assets.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000370" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000370_dcnt_7429c319-3ac4-4aa2-a16d-ddde77494712">
<div style="align:left;">

<td valign="top" style="width:2.5%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.17%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">h)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Goodwill recorded as of December 29, 2019 represented the excess of cost over fair value of net assets acquired in a previous acquisition of the Company&#8217;s predecessor in 2012. Intangible assets include trade names, deferred loan costs, purchased trademarks and liquor licenses at certain restaurants. Goodwill, trade names, trademarks and liquor licenses are not subject to </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">60</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_b63d3152-dfdc-44b0-8925-f2aaf8a3a231" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_a90bf569-0a23-41ec-b0fc-a27454aac6eb"><ix:continuation id="F_000370_dcnt_7429c319-3ac4-4aa2-a16d-ddde77494712">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">amortization, but are tested for impairment annually as of the fiscal year</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8209;end date, or more frequently, if events or changes in circumstances indicate that the asset might be impaired. An impairment loss is recognized to the extent that the carrying amount of the goodwill or indefinite</span><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8209;lived intangible asset exceeds its fair value.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In light of the decline in the market price of the Company&#8217;s common stock, the impact of mandated dining room closures on financial results, the expected reduction in economic activity in the near term, and the general economic and market volatility, the Company determined that these factors constituted an interim triggering event as of the end of each of the Company&#8217;s quarters in fiscal 2020, and performed impairment analyses with regard to its indefinite-lived intangible assets, property and equipment (including its right-of-use assets for operating leases and goodwill. As a result, the Company recorded asset impairment charges totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000441" name="us-gaap:AssetImpairmentCharges" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">16,426</ix:nonFraction> in fiscal year 2020<span style="font-size:11pt;"> </span>related to its goodwill and property and equipment (See Note 2 (i) below).</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company early adopted Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) No. 2017-04, <span style="font-style:italic;">Intangibles &#8211; Goodwill and Other (Topic 350): Simplifying the Test for Goodwill Impairment</span> (&#8220;ASU No. 2017-04&#8221;), which simplifies the subsequent measurement of goodwill by eliminating the second step of the two-step quantitative goodwill impairment test. Impairment was measured at the amount by which the carrying value exceeded the fair value of the reporting unit, not to exceed the carrying value of the reporting unit goodwill. The quantitative goodwill impairment test was performed at the end of the first quarter utilizing a market approach which included observable market prices associated with the Company&#8217;s common stock price in determining a fair value for the Company and its reporting units. As a result of this test, the Company determined that the J. Alexander&#8217;s reporting unit&#8217;s carrying value exceeded its fair value to such an extent that the full impairment of goodwill in the first quarter of 2020 in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000442" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">15,737</ix:nonFraction> was appropriate. The effect of this conclusion is presented as a component of &#8220;Goodwill impairment charge&#8221; on the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company also performed a review of impairment for its other intangible assets at the end of each quarter in 2020, and it was determined that <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000443" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction> impairment of these intangible assets existed in fiscal 2020.&#160;&#160;The same conclusion was reached as of December 29, 2019 and December 30, 2018 during the annual review for impairment in each of these years and, accordingly, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000444" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001617227_20181231_20191229" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000445" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001617227_20180101_20181230" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> impairment losses were recorded.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred loan costs are subject to amortization and are classified in the &#8220;Long-term debt, net of portion classified as current and deferred loan costs&#8221; line item on the Consolidated Balance Sheets. Deferred loan costs are amortized over the life of the related debt.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000371" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOrDisposalOfLongLivedAssetsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000371_dcnt_46174765-9f88-44ff-90e5-6e28d34abbd5">
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:2.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.13%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">i)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Impairment of Long&#8209;Lived Assets</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;)&#160;Topic 360, <span style="font-style:italic;">Property, Plant, and Equipment</span>, long&#8209;lived assets, such as property and equipment and intangible assets subject to amortization, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset or asset group may not be recoverable. Recoverability of assets to be held and used is measured by a comparison of the carrying amount of an asset or asset group to estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated by the asset or asset group. If the carrying amount of an asset or asset group exceeds its estimated undiscounted future cash flows, an impairment charge may be recognized for the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset or asset group exceeds the fair value of the asset or asset group based upon the future highest and best use of the impaired asset or asset group. Fair value is determined by projected future discounted cash flows for each location or the estimated market value of the assets. The asset impairment charges are generally recorded in the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income in the financial statement line item &#8220;Asset impairment charges and restaurant closing costs,&#8221; but are also recorded in the line item &#8220;Loss from discontinued operations, net&#8221; when applicable. Assets to be disposed of are separately presented in the Consolidated Balance Sheets and reported at the lower of carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell and are no longer depreciated.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company recorded a long-lived asset impairment charge of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000446" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" scale="3">689</ix:nonFraction> to state the assets at its Lyndhurst Grill location in Cleveland, Ohio, at their fair value as of the end of the first quarter, which is presented as &#8220;Long-lived asset impairment charges and restaurant closing costs&#8221; on the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income. During the second quarter of 2020, the Company made the decision to permanently close this location after a review of its projected and historical financial performance. This location was also required to be temporarily closed in mid&#8209;March 2020 due to COVID&#8209;19-related traffic limitations unique to that specific restaurant which further impacted operating results. The Company assessed its other restaurant locations for indicators of impairment at the end of each quarter in fiscal year 2020 and assessed recoverability of certain fixed assets as warranted. <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000447" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">No</ix:nonFraction> additional impairment was identified during the year ended January 3, 2021.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000448" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001617227_20181231_20191229" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000449" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001617227_20180101_20181230" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">No</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> impairment charges were recorded for the years ended December 29, 2019 and December 30, 2018.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">61</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_a90bf569-0a23-41ec-b0fc-a27454aac6eb" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_2badb556-d32c-429f-967c-81435ea82b6a"><ix:continuation id="F_000371_dcnt_46174765-9f88-44ff-90e5-6e28d34abbd5">
</ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000372" name="us-gaap:LesseeLeasesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true">
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:2.5%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.17%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">j)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Lease Accounting</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company through its subsidiaries has land only, building only, and land and building leases for a number of its restaurants and its corporate office that are recorded as operating leases.&#160;&#160;The Company determines if an arrangement meets the definition of a lease at inception, at which time it also performs an analysis to determine whether the lease qualifies as operating or financing. Operating leases are included in operating lease right-of-use (&#8220;ROU&#8221;) assets and operating lease current and long-term liabilities on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets. Lease expense for operating leases is generally recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term and is included in other operating expenses (for restaurant properties) or general and administrative expense (for corporate office space) on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income.&#160;&#160;The Company presents both the change in ROU assets and lease liabilities as a single line item in the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows as the change in &#8220;Lease right-of-use assets and liabilities.&#8221; The Company does not currently have any arrangements that are classified as financing leases.&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Most of the Company&#8217;s leases have rent escalation clauses and some have rent holiday and contingent rent provisions.&#160;&#160;Terms for these leases are generally for <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000450" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_c017403b-22fa-4b80-8df1-fd7feb6bdeae">15</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000451" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">20<ix:continuation id="C_c017403b-22fa-4b80-8df1-fd7feb6bdeae"> years</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric> and, in many cases, the leases provide for one or more <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000453">five&#8209;year</span> renewal options.&#160;&#160;As stated, the rent expense under these leases is recognized on a straight&#8209;line basis over an expected lease term, including cancelable option periods when it is reasonably assured that such option periods will be exercised because failure to do so would result in a significant economic penalty, and these periods are recognized as a part of the ROU asset and related lease liability. The Company begins recognizing rent expense on the date that it or its subsidiaries become legally obligated under the lease and take possession of or are given control of the leased property. Rent expense incurred during the construction period for a leased restaurant location is included in pre&#8209;opening expense. Contingent rent expense is generally based upon sales levels and is typically accrued when it is deemed probable that it will be payable.&#160;&#160;These costs are disclosed as variable lease costs.&#160;&#160;Any tenant improvement allowances received from landlords under operating leases are recorded as a reduction to the related ROU asset and lease liability.&#160;&#160;The same lease term that is used to calculate the lease liabilities is also used for assessing leases for finance or operating lease accounting.&#160;&#160;Many of the Company&#8217;s leases require payments for property taxes, insurance, maintenance and certain other costs.&#160;&#160;The variable portion of these payments is not included as a component of the Company&#8217;s ROU assets and lease liabilities.&#160;&#160;Rather, variable payments, other than those dependent on an index or rate, are expensed as incurred and are disclosed as variable lease costs.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certain of the Company&#8217;s leases include both lease (i.e. fixed payments including rent) and non-lease components (e.g., common-area maintenance, marketing, and other miscellaneous fixed costs) which are accounted for as a single lease component as the Company has elected the practical expedient to combine lease and non-lease components for real estate leases. The Company is also a party to leases which have a non-cancelable lease term of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000454" name="jax:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContractDescription" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103">less than&#160;one year</ix:nonNumeric> with no option to purchase the underlying asset&#160;and, therefore, it has elected to exclude these short-term leases from its ROU assets and lease liabilities.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For our existing operating leases that commenced prior to the adoption of ASC Topic 842, <span style="font-style:italic;">Leases</span>, we made an accounting policy election to use the incremental borrowing rate for our leases considering the remaining lease term and remaining minimum rental payments during transition in establishing our lease liabilities.&#160;&#160;For new leases entered into after the adoption of ASC Topic 842, we use an incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at the commencement date in determining the present value of lease payments. The right-of-use asset also includes any lease payments made on or before the commencement date of the lease, less any lease incentives received. As the rate implicit in the lease is not readily determinable in the Company&#8217;s leases, it uses an incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at the lease commencement date in determining the present value of lease payments. The incremental borrowing rates used are estimated based on what the Company would be required to pay for a collateralized loan over a similar term. Additionally, based on the applicable lease terms and the current economic environment, the Company applies a portfolio approach for determining the incremental borrowing rate for its real estate leases.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April 2020, the staff of the FASB issued a question-and-answer document that stated that entities may elect to account for lease concessions related to the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic as though the rights and obligations for those concessions existed as of the commencement of the contract rather than as a lease modification. Lessees may make the election for any lessor-provided lease concession related to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic as long as the concession does not result in a substantial increase in the rights of the lessor or in the obligations of the lessee. The Company has made such elections.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000373" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000373_dcnt_8f626fb6-a11b-4cee-aeb8-c51eec23b249">
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:2.5%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.17%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">k)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Revenue Recognition</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Restaurant sales are recognized at a point in time when food and service are provided to guests at one of the Company&#8217;s restaurants.&#160;Taxes assessed by a governmental authority that are imposed on the Company&#8217;s sales of its food and service and collected by the Company from the guest for remittance to such authorities, are excluded from net sales.&#160;&#160;Further, the Company excludes any discounts, such as management meals and employee meals, associated with each sale.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">62</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_2badb556-d32c-429f-967c-81435ea82b6a" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_19c38738-bb86-411f-808f-b6d03778a68c"><ix:continuation id="F_000373_dcnt_8f626fb6-a11b-4cee-aeb8-c51eec23b249">
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unearned revenue, as separately stated on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheets, represents the contract liability for gift cards, which have been sold but not redeemed. Upon redemption, when the guest presents a gift card as a form of payment for food and service provided at the restaurant, net sales are recorded and the contract liability is redu</span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ced by the amount of card value</span><span style="color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> redeemed.&#160;&#160;The Company considers its performance obligations associated with gift cards sold to guests to be met when food and service have been provided to its guests, and a gift card is presented as a form of payment.&#160;&#160;The amount of gift card revenue that was previously deferred is recognized based on the selling price of the menu items at each restaurant.</span></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Prior to the adoption of ASC Topic 606, <span style="font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers</span>, the Company recorded gift card breakage when such cards were considered to be only remotely likely to be redeemed, and for which there was no legal obligation to remit balances under unclaimed property laws of the relevant jurisdictions.&#160;&#160;Management considered the probability of redemption of a gift card to be remote when it had been outstanding for 24 months. With the adoption of ASC Topic 606 as of January 1, 2018, the Company began analyzing gift card breakage based upon Company-specific historical redemption patterns, and gift card breakage is now recognized as revenue in proportion to guest redemptions.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s gift cards continue to have no expiration date, and it does not deduct non-usage fees from outstanding gift card balances.&#160;&#160;In applying the guidance under this topic, management estimates the percentage of the value of gift cards sold that will go unused by the purchaser of such card,<span style="font-size:12pt;color:#000000;"> </span>and for which there is no legal obligation to remit balances under unclaimed property laws of the relevant jurisdictions, which is a matter of judgement, and, as noted above, recognizes breakage revenue in proportion to actual gift card redemptions during the reporting period, at which time management believes the underlying performance obligations have been satisfied by the Company.&#160;&#160;Gift card breakage is recorded on a quarterly basis in conjunction with the Company&#8217;s preparation of its financial statements and related disclosures and is presented as a component of &#8220;Net sales&#8221; within the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income.&#160;&#160;<span style="color:#000000;">Breakage of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000455" name="jax:RevenueRecognitionGiftCardBreakage" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">422</ix:nonFraction>, $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000456" name="jax:RevenueRecognitionGiftCardBreakage" contextRef="C_0001617227_20181231_20191229" decimals="-3" scale="3">443</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000457" name="jax:RevenueRecognitionGiftCardBreakage" contextRef="C_0001617227_20180101_20181230" decimals="-3" scale="3">378</ix:nonFraction> related to gift cards was recorded in fiscal years 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.</span></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s net sales and net income have historically been subject to seasonal fluctuations. Net sales and operating income typically reach their highest levels during the fourth quarter of the fiscal year due to holiday business and the first quarter of the fiscal year due in part to the redemption of gift cards sold during the holiday season.&#160;&#160;The contract liability relative to gift cards and the recognition of revenue associated with such form of payment is impacted accordingly.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s unearned revenue balance has historically decreased throughout the course of the fiscal year until the fourth quarter when an increase in the balance is typically experienced given the seasonality of gift card sales.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000374" name="jax:VendorRebatesPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true">

<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Transaction costs totaled $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000463" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">645</ix:nonFraction> for fiscal year 2020 and included legal, other professional and consulting fees related to the ongoing evaluation of strategic alternatives. During the first quarter of 2020, the Company announced that given the uncertainties in the business community, the restaurant industry and the financial markets as a result of the COVID-19 </p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">63</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_19c38738-bb86-411f-808f-b6d03778a68c" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_f8273c14-8189-42e4-a654-cdaab8f82a14"><ix:continuation id="F_000376_dcnt_d1c0863e-9c84-4089-8d21-52d55d11436e">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">pandemic, the ongoing review of strategic alternatives by the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors (the &#8220;Board&#8221;) was not expected to be completed until the uncertainties are resolved.</span></p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000377" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true">

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">o)</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Income Taxes</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income taxes are accounted for using the asset and liability method, whereby deferred income taxes reflect the net tax effect of temporary differences between the carrying amounts of assets and liabilities for financial reporting purposes and the amounts used for income tax purposes and for operating loss and tax credit carryforwards. The deferred taxes generated within the J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC partnership are accounted for using the &#8220;outside basis&#8221; approach, and the deferred taxes outside of the partnership are accounted for using the &#8220;inside basis&#8221; approach. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. The effect on deferred tax assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the period that includes the enactment date. Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance if, based on the weight of available evidence, it is more likely than not that the deferred tax assets will not be realized.</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The benefits of uncertain tax positions are recognized in the Consolidated Financial Statements only after determining a more likely than not probability that the uncertain tax positions will withstand challenge, if any, from taxing authorities. When facts and circumstances change, these probabilities are reassessed and any appropriate changes are recorded in the Consolidated Financial Statements. Uncertain tax positions are accounted for by determining the minimum recognition threshold that a tax position is required to meet before being recognized in the Consolidated Financial Statements. This determination requires the use of judgment in assessing the timing and amounts of deductible and taxable items. Tax positions that meet the more likely than not recognition threshold are recognized and measured as the largest amount of tax benefit that is greater than 50% likely of being realized upon settlement with a taxing authority that has full knowledge of all relevant information. Interest and penalties accrued related to unrecognized tax benefits or income tax settlements are recognized as components of income tax expense.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000378" name="us-gaap:ConcentrationRiskCreditRisk" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true">

<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:7pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Concentration of Credit Risk</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Financial instruments that are potentially exposed to a concentration of credit risk are cash and cash equivalents and accounts receivable. Operating cash balances are maintained in noninterest&#8209;bearing transaction accounts, which are insured by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000465" name="us-gaap:CashFDICInsuredAmount" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapCashAndCashEquivalentsAxis_jaxNoninterestBearingDepositsMember_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">250</ix:nonFraction>. Further, a certain portion of the assets held in a rabbi trust established under a retirement benefit arrangement with certain of the Company&#8217;s current and former officers (the &#8220;Trust&#8221;) consists of cash and cash equivalents.&#160;&#160;The Company places cash with high&#8209;credit&#8209;quality financial institutions, and at times, such cash may be in excess of the federally insured limit. However, there have been no losses experienced related to these balances, and the credit risk is believed to be minimal. Also, the Company believes that its risk related to cash equivalents from third&#8209;party credit card issuers for purchases made by guests using the issuers&#8217; credit cards is not significant due to the number of banks involved and the fact that payment is typically received within <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000466" name="jax:PaymentPeriodOnCreditCardTransaction" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20191230_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" continuedAt="C_db4ace35-119f-43a0-b43e-bf23a171f8e9">three</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000467" name="jax:PaymentPeriodOnCreditCardTransaction" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20191230_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">four<ix:continuation id="C_db4ace35-119f-43a0-b43e-bf23a171f8e9"> days</ix:continuation></ix:nonNumeric> of a credit card transaction. Therefore, the Company does not believe it has significant risk related to its cash and cash equivalents accounts.&#160;&#160;Another portion of the assets held in the Trust and the 409a Trust (each defined below) consist of U.S. Treasury bonds as well as a small number of corporate bonds with ratings no lower than BBB. The Company believes the credit risk associated with such bonds to be minimal given the historical stability of the U.S. government and the investment grade bond ratings relative to the corporate issuers.&#160;&#160;Concentrations of credit risk with respect to accounts receivable are related principally to receivables from governmental agencies related to refunds of franchise and income taxes and, in 2020, the ERC under the CARES Act. The Company does not believe it has significant risk related to accounts receivable due to the nature of the entities involved.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000379" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000379_dcnt_2403ae5b-054c-4476-8aee-726db3821eaa">

<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management has made certain estimates and assumptions relating to the reporting of assets and liabilities and the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the Consolidated Financial Statements and the reported amounts of net sales and expenses during the periods presented to prepare these Consolidated Financial Statements in conformity with GAAP. <p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic (loss) earnings per share of common stock is computed by dividing net (loss) income by the weighted average number of shares outstanding for the reporting period.&#160;&#160;Diluted (loss) earnings per share of common stock is computed similarly to basic (loss) earnings per share except the weighted average shares outstanding are increased to include potential shares outstanding resulting from share-based compensation awards and additional shares from the assumed exercise of any common stock equivalents, if dilutive. In periods of net loss, no potential common shares are included in the diluted shares outstanding as the effect is anti-dilutive. J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC Class B Units are considered common stock equivalents for this purpose. The number of additional shares of common stock related to these common stock equivalents is calculated using the if-converted method, if dilutive. The number of additional shares of common stock related to stock option awards and unvested restricted share awards subject to only a service condition is calculated using the treasury stock method, if dilutive. Unvested restricted share awards that are subject to a performance condition are regarded as contingently issuable common shares and are included in the denominator of the diluted earnings per share calculation using the treasury stock method as of the beginning of the period in which the performance condition has been satisfied, if dilutive.&#160;&#160;Refer to Note 3 &#8211; (Loss) Earnings per Share for the basic and diluted (loss) earnings per share calculations and additional discussion.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000386" name="jax:ShareRepurchaseProgramPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000386_dcnt_6072b4f6-a79b-44e5-9ba4-87f22b1a8271">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Recently Issued Accounting Standards</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2016, <span style="color:#000000;">the Financial Accounting Standards Board (the &#8220;FASB&#8221;) </span>issued ASU No. 2016-13, <span style="font-style:italic;">Financial Instruments&#8212;Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments</span> (&#8220;ASU No. 2016-13&#8221;).&#160;&#160;ASU No. 2016-13 was issued to update the methodology used to measure current expected credit losses (&#8220;CECL&#8221;). The update applies to financial assets measured at amortized cost, including loans, held-to-maturity debt securities, net investments in leases, and trade accounts receivable as well as certain off-balance sheet credit exposures, such as loan commitments. This ASU replaces the current incurred loss impairment methodology with a methodology to reflect CECL and requires consideration of a broader range of reasonable and supportable information to explain credit loss estimates.&#160;&#160;ASU No. 2016-13 must be adopted using a modified retrospective transition method through a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings in the period of adoption. The effective date relative to smaller reporting companies is for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2022 and interim periods within those fiscal years. Early adoption is permitted. The Company does not expect the adoption of ASU No. 2016-13 to have a material impact on its Consolidated Financial Statements and related disclosures.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="HH_1">In December 2019, the FASB issued ASU 2019-12, <span style="font-style:italic;">Income Taxes (Topic 740):&#160;Simplifying&#160;the&#160;Accounting&#160;for&#160;Income Taxes</span> (&#8220;ASU No. 2019-12&#8221;). ASU No. 2019-12&#160;simplifies&#160;the&#160;accounting&#160;for&#160;income taxes&#160;by removing certain exceptions to the general principles in Topic 740&#59; amending the interim-period accounting for enacted changes in tax law&#59; and amending the requirements related to the accounting for &#8220;hybrid&#8221; tax regimes. This standard is effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2020, including interim periods within those annual periods, with early adoption permitted. The Company is currently assessing the potential impact of ASU No. 2019-12 on its Consolidated Financial Statements and related disclosures.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:6.67%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In March 2020, the FASB issued ASU No. 2020-04, Reference Rate Reform (Topic 848) (&#8220;ASU No. 2020-04&#8221;).&#160;&#160;This update provides optional expedients and exceptions for applying GAAP to contracts, hedging relationships, and other transactions affected by reference rate reform if certain criteria are met.&#160;&#160;The amendments in ASU No. 2020-04 apply only to contracts, hedging relationships, and other transactions that reference LIBOR or another reference rate expected to be discontinued because of reference rate reform.&#160;&#160;An entity may elect to apply the amendments for contract modifications by the impacted ASC topic as of any date from the beginning of an interim period that includes or is subsequent to March 12, 2020, or prospectively from a date within an interim period that includes or is subsequent to March 12, 2020, up to the date that the financial statements are available to be issued through December 31, 2022. Once elected for an ASC topic, the amendments in ASU No. 2020-04 must be applied prospectively for all eligible contract modifications for that ASC topic.&#160;&#160;The Company has not adopted and continues to assess the potential impact of ASU No. 2020-04 on its Consolidated Financial Statements and related disclosures.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic (loss) earnings per share of common stock is computed by dividing net (loss) income by the weighted average number of shares outstanding for the reporting period.&#160;&#160;Diluted (loss) earnings per share of common stock gives effect during the reporting period to all dilutive potential shares outstanding resulting from share-based compensation awards and additional shares from the assumed exercise of any common stock equivalents, if dilutive.&#160;&#160;The Company incurred a net loss for the year ended January 3, 2021, and therefore, diluted shares outstanding equaled basic shares outstanding.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The J.
