The </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000531" name="jax:NumberOfShareBasedCompensationUnvestedAwardsIncludedInComputationOfEarningsPerShare" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_20181231_20191229" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">264,000</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> unvested restricted share awards outstanding as of </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December 29, 2019</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> were considered dilutive for the 2019 fiscal year and the impact on the number of weighted average shares in the diluted earnings per share calculation was </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000532" name="jax:DilutiveSecuritiesIncludedInComputationOfEarningsPerShareAmount" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_20181231_20191229" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">3,427</ix:nonFraction></span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</span></p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of January 3, 2021 and December 29, 2019, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000533" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20210103" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000534" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsNonvestedNumber" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20191229" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">52,500</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> performance share awards outstanding. Performance share awards are regarded as contingently issuable common shares and are included in the weighted average shares outstanding for basic earnings per share calculation purposes as of the beginning of the period in which the performance condition has been satisfied and the awards have vested. For diluted earnings per share calculation purposes under the treasury stock method, such performance share awards are included in the number of weighted average shares outstanding as of the beginning of the period in which the performance condition has been satisfied, if dilutive.  The performance condition associated with such awards had not been met at either January 3, 2021 and December 29, 2019, and, therefore, the portion of the awards that had satisfied the applicable service condition at each of these reporting dates were excluded from the weighted average shares outstanding for basic (loss) earnings per share calculations.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000344" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000344_dcnt_62dfe680-e907-46f3-98d3-34bb885313ab">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 4 &#8211; Fair Value Measurements</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of January 3, 2021 and December 29, 2019, the fair value of cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivable, accounts payable, accrued expenses and other current liabilities approximated their carrying value due to their short-term nature. The carrying amounts of long-term debt approximate fair value as interest rates and negotiated terms and conditions are consistent with current market rates because of the close proximity of recent refinancing transactions to the dates of these Consolidated Financial Statements (Level 2).</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company utilizes the following fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs into valuation techniques used to measure fair value. Accordingly, the Company uses valuation techniques which maximize the use of observable inputs and minimize the use of unobservable inputs when determining fair value. The three levels of the hierarchy are as follows:</p>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.17%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;1</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Defined as observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.17%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:0pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;2</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Defined as observable inputs other than Level&#160;1 prices. These include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in an active market, quoted prices for identical assets or liabilities in markets that are not active, or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets or liabilities.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:9.2%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level&#160;3</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:12pt;margin-top:12pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">Defined as unobservable inputs for which little or no market data exists, therefore, requiring an entity to develop its own assumptions about the assumptions that market participants would use in pricing the asset or liability, including assumptions about risk.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets and Liabilities Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first quarter of fiscal year 2020, primarily due to the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Company determined that a triggering event had occurred requiring an impairment evaluation of its long-lived assets, indefinite&#8209;lived intangible assets and goodwill. As a result of these analyses, the Company recorded a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000535" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfLongLivedAssetsToBeDisposedOf" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" scale="3">689</ix:nonFraction> impairment charge related to the long-lived assets at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxRestaurant" id="F_000536" name="jax:NumberOfRestaurantsClosed" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20200329" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> restaurant location that management determined would be permanently closed (i.e., Lyndhurst Grill in Cleveland, Ohio) and a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000537" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">15,737</ix:nonFraction> impairment charge related to the Company&#8217;s recorded goodwill. The impairment charges were measured based on the amounts by which the carrying values of the assets exceeded their relative fair values. <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000538" name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsIndefinitelivedExcludingGoodwill" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">No</ix:nonFraction> impairment was recorded for indefinite&#8209;lived intangible assets as their fair values were determined to substantially exceed their carrying values. Fair values for goodwill and long-lived assets that were impaired during fiscal year 2020 were estimated utilizing a market approach, and fair value estimates for indefinite-lived intangibles were determined based on an income approach. Fair value estimates utilized market participant assumptions reflecting all available information as of the impairment date. The fair value of goodwill was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000539" name="jax:RemainingCarryingValueOfGoodwillAfterImpairment" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapFairValueByFairValueHierarchyLevelAxis_us-gaapFairValueInputsLevel3Member_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" scale="3">0</ix:nonFraction> (Level 3), and the Lyndhurst Grill location was sold during the third quarter of 2020 and therefore has <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000540" name="jax:RemainingBookValueOfLongLivedAssetsAfterSaleOfLocation" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_stprOH_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction> remaining value on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Balance Sheet as of January 3, 2021. There were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000541" name="jax:NonFinancialAssetsMeasuredAtFairValue" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapFairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_us-gaapFairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember_20191229" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000542" name="jax:NonFinancialAssetsMeasuredAtFairValue" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapFairValueByMeasurementFrequencyAxis_us-gaapFairValueMeasurementsNonrecurringMember_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="3">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> non-financial assets measured at fair value on a non&#8209;recurring basis as of January 3, 2021 or December 29, 2019.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">68</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;text-align:justify;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash and cash equivalents are classified as Level 1 of the fair value hierarchy as they represent cash held in the Trust.&#160;&#160;Cash held in the Trust is invested through an overnight repurchase agreement the investments of which may include U.S. Treasury securities, such as bonds or Treasury bills, and other agencies of the U.S. government.&#160;&#160;Such investments are valued using quoted market prices in active markets.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. government obligations held in the Trust include U.S. Treasury Bonds.&#160;&#160;These bonds as well as the corporate bonds listed above are considered to be trading securities and are classified as Level 1 of the fair value hierarchy given their readily available quoted prices in active markets.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At January 3, 2021 and December 29, 2019, the Company held investments in mutual and money market funds classified as trading securities that were also held in a rabbi trust as of January 3, 2021 (the &#8220;409a Trust&#8221;) to support its future obligations to participants of its nonqualified deferred compensation plan, which are carried at fair value based on quoted market prices in active markets for identical assets (Level 1).</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At January 3, 2021 and December 28, 2019, the Company held life insurance policies in the Trust that are recorded at cash surrender value.&#160;&#160;The value of each policy was determined by MassMutual Financial Group, an A-rated insurance company, which provides the value of these policies to the Company on a regular basis.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were no transfers between the levels listed above during either of the reporting periods.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Unrealized gains or losses on investments held in either the Trust or the 409a Trust are presented as a component of &#8220;Other, net&#8221; on the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income.&#160;&#160;The assets of both the Trust and the 409a Trust disclosed above are presented as a component of &#8220;Other assets&#8221; on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</p></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:7pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 10 &#8211; Debt</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Current Loan Agreement</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is party to the Fourth Amended and Restated Loan Agreement (the &#8220;Fourth Loan Agreement&#8221;) with Pinnacle Bank, dated October 28, 2020. The Fourth Loan Agreement amended and restated the Company&#8217;s Third Amended and Restated Loan Agreement (the &#8220;Third Loan Agreement&#8221;) entered into on June 5, 2020, and the Third Loan Agreement amended and restated in its entirety the Company&#8217;s Second Amended and Restated Loan Agreement (the &#8220;Second Loan Agreement&#8221;), dated May 20, 2015. The borrower under the Fourth Loan Agreement is J. Alexander&#8217;s, LLC, and it is guaranteed by J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC and all of its significant subsidiaries. The indebtedness outstanding under this Fourth Loan Agreement is secured by liens on certain personal property of the Company and its subsidiaries, subsidiary guarantees, and a mortgage lien on certain real property. The Fourth Loan Agreement, among other things, permits payments of tax dividends to members, restricts liens and encumbrances, restricts dividends, and contains certain other provisions customarily included in such agreements. The Fourth Loan Agreement consists of the following:<span style="margin-left:36pt;"></span></p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">COVID-19 Response and Loan Modifications and Amendments</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the first quarter of 2020, the Company announced it drew down the remaining $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000657" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromLongTermLinesOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_jaxDevelopmentLineOfCreditMember_20191230_20200329" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">17,000</ix:nonFraction> of available capacity (at the time of the draw) under the Development Line of Credit and the Revolving Line of Credit (the &#8220;Credit Draw&#8221;). The Credit Draw was undertaken as a precautionary measure to provide increased liquidity and preserve financial flexibility in light of the disruption and uncertainty resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic. Following the Credit Draw, debt outstanding under the Development Line of Credit and the Revolving Line of Credit totaled $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000658" name="us-gaap:LineOfCredit" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapCreditFacilityAxis_us-gaapRevolvingCreditFacilityMember_us-gaapLongtermDebtTypeAxis_jaxDevelopmentLineOfCreditMember_20200329" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">21,000</ix:nonFraction>. <p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 13 - Leases</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company adopted ASC Topic 842, Leases, as of the first day of fiscal year 2019, December 31, 2018, electing the optional transition method to apply the standard as of the effective date. Accordingly, the Company recorded a cumulative-effect adjustment to opening retained earnings for the impairment of an abandoned ROU asset at the effective date for a restaurant that was previously impaired and the remaining lease payments were accounted for under ASC Topic 420, Exit or Disposal Obligations, as shown in the Consolidated Statement of Shareholders&#8217; Equity. Additionally, the adoption of Topic 842 had a material impact on the Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities as a result of the recognition of operating lease ROU assets and lease liabilities on its Consolidated Balance Sheets. The adoption of Topic 842 did not have a material effect on the Company&#8217;s Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income and Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of January 3, 2021, the Company is party to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxLease" id="F_000731" name="jax:NumberOfRealEstatePropertiesUnderOperatingLeasesAtAdoption" contextRef="C_0001617227_20181230" decimals="INF">30</ix:nonFraction> separate operating leases for real estate on which it currently operates its restaurants and has its corporate office space and remains a party to one operating lease for a closed location. Additionally, d<span style="color:#000000;">uring fiscal year 2020, the Company took possession of the new restaurant location in San Antonio, Texas, and the Redlands Grill location is slated to open in March 2021. Further, the Company entered into a lease for a new restaurant location in Madison, Alabama, which it anticipates will open during the fourth quarter of 2021 but for which it has not yet taken possession. </span><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;color:#000000;">The commencement date of the Madison, Alabama, location has been delayed from the previously anticipated date due to the Company&#8217;s decision to limit capital expenditures in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.</span><span style="color:#000000;">&#160;Each of the leases for the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxLease" id="F_000732" name="jax:OperatingLeasesForRealEstateProperties" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> new locations include a lease term, including option periods, of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000734" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" format="ixt-sec:duryear">30</ix:nonNumeric> years. The Company is also party to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxLease" id="F_000733" name="jax:NumberOfEquipmentLeaseEntered" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">one</ix:nonFraction> equipment operating lease.</span></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company modified certain of its leases during fiscal year 2020 for matters unrelated to the COVID-19 pandemic and updated the ROU assets, lease liabilities and related incremental borrowing rates as required.</p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During fiscal year 2020, the Company was granted COVID-19 related rent concessions for 16 of its restaurant locations and for its corporate office. Under these landlord agreements, certain rent payments will be deferred for various periods, generally providing for <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000735" name="jax:PercentageOfRentPaymentDeferralsAssociatedWithCOVID19LandlordGrantedRentConcessions" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% rent deferral ranging between three to six months.&#160;&#160;Certain other locations received rent abatements ranging from <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000736" name="jax:PercentageOfRentPaymentDeferralsAssociatedWithCOVID19LandlordGrantedRentConcessions" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% to the full amount of the original lease amount for a period of three to seven months.&#160;&#160;The Company has elected to account for lease concessions resulting directly from COVID-19 as though the enforceable rights and obligations to the concessions existed in the respective agreements at lease inception and will not account for the concessions as lease modifications, unless the concession results in a substantial increase in the Company&#8217;s obligations, taking into consideration the guidance issued by the FASB in its Staff question-and-answer document regarding rent concessions related to the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. Of the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxAgreement" id="F_000737" name="jax:NumberOfCovid19RelatedRentConcessionAgreements" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="INF">17</ix:nonFraction> rent concessions, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxAgreement" id="F_000738" name="jax:NumberOfRentConcessionAgreementsQualifiedForSpecialAccountingTreatment" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="INF">15</ix:nonFraction> agreements qualified for this accounting election, and the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxAgreement" id="F_000739" name="jax:NumberOfAgreementsCOVID19RelatedLeaseModifications" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> agreements were treated as lease modifications due to a significant extension to the lease term resulting in a substantial increase in total lease payments associated with each lease. The Company&#8217;s ROU assets and lease liabilities have been remeasured for lease concessions received to take into consideration the impact of the two lease modifications including adjustment for their respective incremental borrowing rates as well as the timing of the aforementioned abatements and deferrals, the impact of which is presented in the information below.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASC Topic 740, <span style="font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</span>, establishes procedures to measure deferred tax assets and liabilities and assess whether a valuation allowance relative to existing deferred tax assets is necessary. Management assesses the likelihood of realization of the Company&#8217;s deferred tax assets and the need for a valuation allowance with respect to those assets based on the weight of available positive and negative evidence. As of January 3, 2021, management determined that a valuation allowance of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000836" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">317</ix:nonFraction> was necessary relative to certain state net operating loss and capital loss carryforwards which are not expected to be realized. Management also determined at January 3, 2021 that it is more likely than not that the results of future operations and reversal of deferred tax liabilities will generate sufficient taxable income to realize the remaining deferred tax assets not covered by this valuation allowance.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of January 3, 2021, the Company has state gross operating loss carryforwards gross of the valuation allowance and uncertain tax positions discussed above of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000837" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsOperatingLossCarryforwardsSubjectToExpiration" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapStateAndLocalJurisdictionMember_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">15,185</ix:nonFraction> <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000838" name="jax:StateGrossOperatingLossCarryForwardsExpirationDates" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103">expiring in years 2021 through 2040</ix:nonNumeric> as well as an additional $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000841" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsOperatingLossCarryforwardsNotSubjectToExpiration" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">3,029</ix:nonFraction> that will never expire. The Company also has federal general business credit carryforwards of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000839" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsTaxCreditCarryforwardsGeneralBusiness" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">7,108</ix:nonFraction> <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000840" name="jax:FederalGeneralBusinessCreditCarryForwardsExpirationDates" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103">expiring in 2031 through 2040</ix:nonNumeric>.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The CARES Act includes several significant income and other business tax provisions that, among other things, eliminates the taxable income limit for certain net operating losses (&#8220;NOLs&#8221;) and allows businesses to carry back NOLs arising in 2018, 2019 and 2020 to the five prior tax years, loosens the business interest limitation under Internal Revenue Code Section 163(j) and fixes the qualified improvement property (&#8220;QIP&#8221;) regulations in the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. As a result of the CARES Act, the Company estimates that it will be able to obtain a $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000842" name="jax:TaxRefundRelatedToCarrybackOfNetOperatingLoss" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapUnusualOrInfrequentItemAxis_jaxCoronavirusAidReliefAndEconomicSecurityActMember_20191230_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">6,856</ix:nonFraction> tax refund from the carryback of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000843" name="us-gaap:OperatingLossCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapIncomeTaxAuthorityAxis_us-gaapDomesticCountryMember_20210103" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">23,761</ix:nonFraction> fiscal 2020 gross federal NOLs, which otherwise would have an indefinite carryforward period.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additionally, the Company has recorded a liability (including interest) in connection with uncertain tax positions related to state tax issues totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000844" name="us-gaap:LiabilityForUncertainTaxPositionsNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">72</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000845" name="us-gaap:LiabilityForUncertainTaxPositionsNoncurrent" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191229" decimals="-3" scale="3">66</ix:nonFraction> as of January 3, 2021 and December 29, 2019, respectively. The Company accrues interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in its provision for income taxes.&#160;&#160;The Company has accrued interest related to unrecognized tax benefits of approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000846" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncomeTaxPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" contextRef="C_0001617227_20210103" decimals="-3" scale="3">6</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000847" name="us-gaap:UnrecognizedTaxBenefitsIncomeTaxPenaltiesAndInterestAccrued" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191229" decimals="-3" scale="3">1</ix:nonFraction> as of January 3, 2021 and December 29, 2019, respectively. </p>

<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, Inc. Amended and Restated 2015 Equity Incentive Plan</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, Inc. Amended and Restated 2015 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;), directors, officers and key employees of the Company may be granted equity incentive awards, such as stock options, restricted stock and stock appreciation rights in an effort to retain qualified management and personnel. The Company&#8217;s Board approved the amended and restated plan in May 2019, and it was subsequently approved by shareholders of the Company in June 2019 at the annual meeting of shareholders. <p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The expected life of stock options granted during the period presented was calculated in accordance with the simplified method described in SEC Staff Accounting Bulletin (&#8220;SAB&#8221;) Topic 14.D.2 in accordance with SAB 110. This approach was utilized due to the lack of exercise history and the anticipated behavior of the overall group of grantees. The risk-free rate for periods within the contractual life of the options is based on the <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000881">five-year</span> U.S. Treasury bond rate in effect at the time of grant. The Company utilized a weighted rate for expected volatility based on a representative peer group within the industry. The dividend yield was set at zero as the underlying security does not pay a dividend. Additionally, management has made an accounting policy election to account for forfeitures when they occur.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In fiscal 2020 and 2019, the Company granted <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000960" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_20191230_20210103" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">63,000</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000961" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_20181231_20191229" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">264,000</ix:nonFraction> restricted share awards, respectively, under the Plan to members of its Board in 2020, and, in 2019, to members of the Board and certain employees of the Company. Also, in fiscal 2019, <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000962" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardEquityInstrumentsOtherThanOptionsGrantsInPeriod" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapPerformanceSharesMember_20181231_20191229" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">52,500</ix:nonFraction> performance share awards were granted to certain employees of the Company under the Plan. Restricted share awards are subject to only a service condition while performance share awards are regarded as contingently issuable common shares which are dependent upon achievement of certain performance targets by the Company. With respect to the restricted share awards, the restricted period for the 2019 grant is <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000963" name="jax:ShareBasedCompensationRestrictedPeriodForGrantingShares" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_20181231_20191229" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">four years</ix:nonNumeric> with the restriction expiring in <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_jaxInstallment" id="F_000964" name="jax:NumberOfInstallments" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_20181231_20191229" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">four</ix:nonFraction> equal installments on the first four anniversaries of their respective grant dates. For the 2020 restricted share award grant, the vesting period is <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000965" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingPeriod1" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_us-gaapRestrictedStockMember_20191230_20210103" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> from the date of the grant. For the performance share awards, the performance period shall be any four consecutive fiscal quarters during the sixteen-quarter period beginning with the fiscal quarter in which the awards were granted. The performance target must be met for the performance period in order for the restriction to lapse.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000410" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfNonvestedShareActivityTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapAwardTypeAxis_jaxRestrictedStockAndPerformanceSharesMember_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000410_cnt_1">

<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management Profits Interest Plan</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 1, 2015, J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC adopted its 2015 Management Incentive Plan and granted equity incentive awards to certain members of its management in the form of Class B Units. The Class B Units are profits interests in J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC. Class B Units in the amount of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000993" name="jax:CommonStockCapitalSharesAuthorizedAndReservedForFutureIssuance" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_jaxManagementProfitsInterestPlanMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20150101" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">1,770,000</ix:nonFraction> were reserved for issuance under the plan and a total of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_000994" name="us-gaap:CommonUnitIssued" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_jaxManagementProfitsInterestPlanMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20150101" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">885,000</ix:nonFraction> Class B Units were granted on January 1, 2015. Each Class B Unit represents a non-voting equity interest in J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC that entitles the holder to a percentage of the profits and appreciation in the equity value of J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC arising after the date of grant and after such time as an applicable hurdle amount is met. The hurdle amount for the Class B Units issued to our management in January 2015 was set at $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000995" name="jax:HurdleRateManagementProfitsInterestGrant" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_jaxManagementProfitsInterestPlanMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20150101" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">180,000</ix:nonFraction>, which at such time was a reasonable premium to the estimated liquidation value of the equity of J.&#160;Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC. The Class B Units issued to management vested with respect to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000996" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_jaxManagementProfitsInterestPlanMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_us-gaapVestingAxis_us-gaapShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheOneMember_20141231_20150101" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% of the grant units on the second anniversary of the date of grant and with respect to the remaining <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000997" name="us-gaap:SharebasedCompensationArrangementBySharebasedPaymentAwardAwardVestingRightsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_jaxManagementProfitsInterestPlanMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_us-gaapVestingAxis_us-gaapShareBasedCompensationAwardTrancheTwoMember_20141231_20150101" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% on the third anniversary of the date of grant and required a <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000998">six-month</span> holding period post vesting.</p>

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The member equity price per unit was based on an enterprise valuation of J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC divided by the number of Class A Units outstanding at the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The Class B hurdle price is based on the hurdle rate divided by the number of Class A Units outstanding at the time of grant. The expected life of management profits interest awards granted during the period presented was determined based on the vesting term of the award which also includes a six-month holding period subsequent to meeting the requisite vesting period. The risk-free rate for periods within the contractual life of the profit interest award is based on an extrapolated four-year U.S. Treasury bond rate in effect at the time of grant given the expected time to liquidity. The Company utilized a weighted rate for expected volatility based on a representative peer group of comparable public companies. The dividend yield was set at <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001008" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardFairValueAssumptionsExpectedDividendRate" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapPlanNameAxis_jaxManagementProfitsInterestPlanMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20141231_20150101" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="-2">zero</ix:nonFraction> as the underlying security does not pay a dividend. The protective put method was used to estimate the discount for lack of marketability inherent to the awards due to the lack of liquidity associated with the post-vesting requirement and other restrictions on the Class B Units.</p>

<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 16 &#8211;<span style="font-weight:normal;"> </span>Other Employee Benefits</p>
<p style="text-align:left;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:10pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A subsidiary of the Company maintains a Savings Incentive and Salary Deferral Plan under Section&#160;401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code (the&#160;&#8220;401(k) Plan&#8221;) for the benefit of its employees and their beneficiaries. <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001027" name="us-gaap:DescriptionOfDefinedContributionPensionAndOtherPostretirementPlans" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_jaxFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20191230_20210103">Under the 401(k) Plan, qualifying employees can defer a portion of their income on a pretax basis through contributions to the 401(k) Plan, subject to an annual statutory limit. <p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Voting rights.<span style="font-style:normal;"> The holders of common stock as well as restricted and performance share awards are entitled to one vote per share on all matters to be voted upon by the shareholders.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Dividend rights.<span style="font-style:normal;"> Subject to preferences that may be applicable to any outstanding preferred stock, the holders of shares of common stock are entitled to receive ratably such dividends, if any, as may be declared from time to time by the Board out of funds legally available therefor.&#160;&#160;Holders of restricted and performance share awards are entitled to dividend rights once such shares have vested.&#160;&#160;Prior to vesting, dividends may be accumulated for eventual payment once relevant restrictions have expired or performance targets are met by the Company, as applicable.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Rights upon liquidation.<span style="font-style:normal;"> In the event of any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of affairs, the holders of common stock are entitled to share ratably in all assets remaining after payment of debts and other liabilities, subject to prior distribution rights of preferred stock then outstanding, if any.&#160;&#160;Such rights are conferred upon holders of restricted or performance share awards upon vesting.</span></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other rights.<span style="font-style:normal;"> The holders of common stock as well as restricted and performance share awards have no preemptive or conversion rights or other subscription rights. Further, there are no redemption or sinking fund provisions applicable to the common stock or the aforementioned awards. The rights, preferences and privileges of holders of common stock and vested restricted and performance share awards will be subject to those of the holders of any shares of preferred stock the Company may issue in the future.</span></p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000358" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000358_dcnt_0f96f6de-6993-43a5-b7bb-2b73e3956be1">

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is subject to real property, personal property, business, franchise and income, payroll and sales and use taxes in various jurisdictions within the United States and is regularly under audit by tax authorities. <p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company and its subsidiaries are defendants from time to time in various claims or legal proceedings arising in the ordinary course of business, including claims relating to workers&#8217; compensation matters, labor-related claims, discrimination and similar matters, claims resulting from guest accidents while visiting a restaurant, claims relating to lease and contractual obligations, federal and state tax matters, and claims from guests or employees alleging illness, injury or other food quality, health or operational concerns, and injury or wrongful death under &#8220;dram shop&#8221; laws that allow a person to sue the Company based on any injury caused by an intoxicated person who was wrongfully served alcoholic beverages at one of its restaurants.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management does not believe that any of the legal proceedings pending against it as of the date of this report will have a material adverse effect on its liquidity, results of operations or financial condition. The Company may incur liabilities, receive benefits, settle disputes, sustain judgments, or accrue expenses relating to legal proceedings in a particular fiscal year, which may adversely affect its results of operations, or on occasion, receive settlements that favorably affect its results of operations.</p></ix:nonNumeric>

</ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000359" name="us-gaap:RelatedPartyTransactionsDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true">
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Note 19 &#8211; Related-Party Transactions</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On September 28, 2015, J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC entered into the Management Consulting Agreement with Black Knight, pursuant to which Black Knight provided corporate and strategic advisory services to J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC. On <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001071" name="jax:ManagementConsultingAgreementTerminationDate" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_jaxBlackKnightAdvisoryServicesLLCMember_20181129_20181130" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">November 30, 2018</ix:nonNumeric>, the Company terminated the Management Consulting Agreement by entering into the Termination Agreement.&#160;&#160;The details pertaining to the termination of this agreement are discussed below.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Under the Management Consulting Agreement, J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC issued Black Knight non-voting Class B Units and was required to pay Black Knight an annual fee equal to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001072" name="jax:AnnualManagementConsultingFeeAsPercentageOfEarningsBeforeIncomeTaxDepreciationAmortization" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_jaxBlackKnightAdvisoryServicesLLCMember_20180101_20181230" decimals="2" scale="-2">3</ix:nonFraction>% of the Company&#8217;s Adjusted EBITDA for each fiscal year during the term of the Management Consulting Agreement. J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC also reimbursed Black Knight for its direct out-of-pocket costs incurred for management services provided to J. Alexander&#8217;s Holdings, LLC. Under the Management Consulting Agreement, &#8220;Adjusted EBITDA&#8221; meant the Company&#8217;s net income (loss) before interest expense, income tax (expense) benefit, depreciation and amortization, and adding asset impairment charges and restaurant closing costs, loss on disposals of fixed assets, transaction and integration costs, non-cash compensation, loss from discontinued operations, gain on debt extinguishment, pre-opening costs and certain unusual items.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Termination Agreement, in the first quarter of 2019, the Company paid approximately $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001073" name="us-gaap:PaymentForManagementFee" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_jaxBlackKnightAdvisoryServicesLLCMember_20181231_20190331" decimals="-3" scale="3">705</ix:nonFraction> to Black Knight which represented the pro-rata portion of its consulting fees earned during 2018 through the Termination Date.  Additionally, the early termination of the Management Consulting Agreement required the cash payment of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001074" name="jax:PaymentOfTerminationFee" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_jaxBlackKnightAdvisoryServicesLLCMember_20190130_20190131" decimals="-3" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" scale="3">4,560</ix:nonFraction> to Black Knight as a termination fee which the Company paid on January 31, 2019 using cash on hand.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During fiscal years 2018, management fees and reimbursable out-of-pocket costs of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001075" name="us-gaap:ManagementFeeExpense" contextRef="C_0001617227_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_us-gaapGeneralAndAdministrativeExpenseMember_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_jaxBlackKnightAdvisoryServicesLLCMember_20180101_20181230" decimals="-3" scale="3">703</ix:nonFraction> were incurred relative to the Black Knight Management Consulting Agreement. Such costs are presented as a component of &#8220;General and administrative expenses&#8221; on the Consolidated Statements of Operations and Comprehensive (Loss) Income.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;">The Class B Units granted to Black Knight vested in equal installments on the first, second, and third anniversaries of the October 6, 2015 grant date and were measured at fair value at each reporting date through the date of vesting. Under the terms of the Termination Agreement, Black Knight had <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001076" name="jax:CommonUnitsExchangePeriodUponTermination" contextRef="C_0001617227_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_jaxBlackKnightAdvisoryServicesLLCMember_us-gaapStatementClassOfStockAxis_us-gaapCommonClassBMember_20150926_20150928" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> days from November 30, 2018 to exchange its Class B Units to exercise its right to convert the value of such units above the applicable hurdle rate to the Company&#8217;s common stock.&#160;&#160;Since Black Knight did not exercise its conversion rights within the 90-day period, the Class B Units were cancelled and forfeited for no consideration on February 28, 2019.</span></p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000360" name="us-gaap:MinorityInterestDisclosureTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001617227_20191230_20210103" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000360_dcnt_feb23b67-abb9-4551-a463-d69d367d0ddf">

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:6.67%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None.</p>

<div style="align:left;">

<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.33%;white-space:nowrap">

<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><span style="Background-color:#auto;text-decoration:none;"></span><span style="color:#000000;"></span><span style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Evaluation of disclosure controls and procedures</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s principal executive officer and principal financial officer have conducted an evaluation of the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Exchange Act Rule 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e)) as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report. Based on that evaluation, the Company&#8217;s principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that, as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report, the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures were effective as of such date. Our disclosure controls and procedures are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in the reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms and that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:7.87%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:left;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;color:#auto;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;letter-spacing:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><span style="Background-color:#auto;text-decoration:none;"></span><span style="color:#000000;"></span><span style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</span></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting, as defined in Rule 13a-15(f) under the Exchange Act. Management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, has assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report based on the framework established in &#8220;Internal Control&#8212;Integrated Framework (2013)&#8221;, issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Based on this evaluation, management has concluded that the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting was effective as of the end of the period covered by this Annual Report.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our system of internal control over financial reporting was designed to provide reasonable assurance regarding the preparation and fair presentation of published financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. All internal control systems, no matter how well designed, have inherent limitations. Therefore, even those systems determined to be effective can provide only reasonable assurance and may not prevent or detect misstatements. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may deteriorate.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:3.33%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">This Annual Report does not include an attestation report of our independent registered public accounting firm, KPMG LLP, regarding internal control over financial reporting. We were not required to have, nor have we, engaged KPMG LLP to perform an audit of internal control over financial reporting pursuant to the rules of the Commission that permit us to provide only management&#8217;s report in this Annual Report.</p>
